item.title: Site-Competition–Driven Synergistic Li+/Na+ Transport in Li5₋xNaxLa3Ta2O12: The 3:1 Optimum
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study reveals that in mixed-cation Li5₋xNaxLa3Ta2O12 garnets, a 3:1 Li:Na ratio yields optimal ionic conductivity via site-competition-driven synergistic Li+/Na+ transport. It clarifies how competing alkali species interact and provides a design principle for enhancing conductivity in solid electrolytes without extrinsic dopants, advancing understanding of mixed-cation ion-transport mechanisms for battery applications.

item.description:

💡 Pantolactone is introduced as a multifunctional electrolyte additive that forms a molecular-bridge interface layer on the Zn anode while coordinating Zn2+ to reconstruct its solvation sheath. This dual strategy accelerates desolvation, guides Zn(002) deposition, and suppresses water activity and side reactions, enabling over 3400 h cycling and 94.1% capacity retention, offering a new paradigm coupling interfacial engineering with solvation regulation for AZIBs.

💡 The novelty lies in precisely tuning carbon defect density to reveal a linear correlation with NO₃RR activity, uncovering how defects break interfacial hydrogen-bond ordering to accelerate water dissociation and enable an adsorbed-H mediated pathway.
